title: Ice skating as a boy and on the road
summary: He tells of boyhood skating and of skating with the band behind a gymnasium.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Jesus... I used to skate like crazy all winter, you know. And I graduated from regular skates to box-toes to racers, and I had 18-inch racers. And I could really handle 'em. There was a pond about a half to three-quarters of a mile from my house that used to freeze over every winter, and we used to all skate there. And we'd leave our skates there on the way to school in the morning, and stash them under a bush. That was when things were safe, 1924 or '25. And boy, I'd come back after school and throw my books in the bushes, put on those racers, and away we'd go! Skating.

So now, we go out with Jerry Gray, we go to a place where... We played behind a gymnasium. And out in front of the gymnasium was an ice-skating rink. And this girl was doing pirouettes and everything; you know, she was practicing the figure skating. And Al Hendrickson(?), the guitar player, turned around, and he was doin' this, you

know -- and every time he did it, why, he'd flip his guitar. You know, I could always tell when he was stoned. He'd flip his guitar, you know, completely over, and bust everybody up. And he flipped that a couple of times, and finally he turned around to me and he says, "Skates her dick off, doesn't she." [LAUGHS]

So when it was all over, we went out, and all the guys in the band decided they wanted to skate. So I got some racers. [SIPS] Well, if you're gonna skate good, you've got to skate all the time, because your ankles get weak. And I hadn't skated for fifteen, twenty years almost. And I went out there, and I started in with my stuff, and my ankles weren't any good.

But I soon overcame that, and the first thing you know, I was the star of the show, skating circles around these guys. Nobody knew how to skate but me! And I'd stand up on my toes, you know, on 18-inch racers, and off I'd go, and up in the air and come down and all that jazz... Boy, they just thought I was sumpin' else. Them skates. Heh, I had to put two pairs of socks on, and then double the sock one sock down so that my ankles were stronger. I used to love to ice skate.
You had long winters up there in Washington.
Yeah. And you don't have to skate in a

circle like you do, like, in Central Park here or wherever they've got these skating rinks. It's round and round she goes. And if you want to do anything, you've got to go out in the middle and do a Figure-Eight or some damn thing. That's bullshit! Ice skating is ice skating. You really go when you skate. You make sudden stops and jerks and turns and whirls -- that's skatin'! Like hockey players. I mean, that's an ice skater. He ain't one of these guys that puts his hand behind his back and goes...you know, that stuff. That's bullshit. It's good. But compared to... You put one of those distance skaters in a hockey game, they'd carry him out on a stretcher in five seconds.
